A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Geometry Forcing. Their complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RealEstate10K and Minecraft experiments, representation and loss ablations, geometric reconstruction probes, qualitative comparisons, and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds teacher and alignment ablations, text-to-video results, computational profiling, and failure-case evidence.

M1.justification: The angular and scale alignment objectives, combined training loss, and core generation framework remain unchanged. Pi3 and Wan2.1 experiments test the existing approach; newly specified projectors and preprocessing do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Alongside retained RealEstate10K camera-conditioned and Minecraft action-conditioned tasks, Appendix D.5 adds general text-conditioned video generation using 2,000 SpatialVid videos. This introduces a distinct conditioning task and additional real-world video coverage.

E2.justification: The main DFoT, REPA, VideoREPA, Cosmos, and NFD comparators remain. The ControlNet comparison changes from conditioning on VGGT features to conditioning on rendered images from reconstructed geometry. New comparisons also include alternative Pi3 supervision and Wan2.1-1.3B without GF.

E3.justification: New experimental designs vary alignment context across 4, 8, and 16 frames, compare middle-layer with last-three-layer alignment, and evaluate Wan2.1-1.3B using aesthetic quality, imaging quality, and motion smoothness. Existing main settings remain stated, but Appendix C.2 introduces an unreconciled two-epoch/global-batch-40 description alongside Section 5's 2,500 steps/batch 8; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F add teacher-model, context-length, and simultaneous-layer ablations; computational profiling; a reflective-glass failure case; and qualitative evidence about scale alignment. The external-geometry ablation is substantively revised and expanded beyond FVD. Existing representation, loss, alignment-depth, and exposure-bias analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for these experiments. The additional tables and plots retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5–6 retain their numerical results. Table 4 replaces the feature-conditioned ControlNet result, FVD 275, with a differently configured rendered-geometry comparison, FVD 280; this is not a same-setting regression. New results include Pi3-teacher FVD 309, context-length FVDs 261/257/243, Wan2.1 imaging quality 0.56 versus 0.59 with GF, and timing/FLOP measurements.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, alignment losses, combined objective, and reprojection-error definition are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the new mechanism discussions are interpretive.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: geometric representation alignment through angular and scale objectives improves video quality and consistency. The additional appendix experiments support broader applicability without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of static-teacher limitations in dynamic scenes, reflective-material failures, computational tradeoffs, teacher requirements, and a geometric explanation for reduced exposure bias. Appendix E.2 argues that geometric and semantic representations overlap, although Section 5.3 still calls them orthogonal, creating an internal inconsistency.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies Conv3D and separate projectors, 512×512 interpolation, 10,000 training clips, and 50-step DDIM sampling; Appendix E adds A800 profiling information. Conversely, v1's Cosmos model/chunking instructions and VideoMAEv2-based baseline construction details disappear. New training disclosures are not reconciled with the retained main-text settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds SpatialVid and Pi3 references and removes the VideoMAE v2 reference with its baseline-description paragraph. The central positioning relative to REPA, geometric foundation models, and consistent world modeling remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The supplement is substantially reorganized from A.1–A.3 into sections A–F with a contents list and separate implementation, experiment, discussion, and visualization sections. v2 also adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements and extensively condenses or edits introductory, related-work, and explanatory prose, while retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–12 and new computational, failure-case, and scale-alignment displays in Figures 5, 6, and 8. Existing tables and figures are relocated or resized, and captions are revised. v1 Figure 5 survives as v2 Figure 7; Figures 3–4 retain the same plotted content.

improvement.justification: The added teacher/design controls, text-to-video test, resource measurements, and concrete failure case make the unchanged method easier to assess. These benefits support a modest net improvement. However, conflicting training descriptions, contradictory representation interpretations, and removal of useful baseline implementation details limit reproducibility and clarity, preventing a stronger improvement judgment.
